quote: This definition does not incorporate the "other than the Excluded Assets" limitation found in APA § 2.1. ... Bill of Sale § 2.1, which conveys "all of the Purchased Assets," would transfer to Buyer: The HOLLIS trademark ... The Albany manufacturing facility ... Seller's cash ... Replace Bill of Sale § 1.1(b) with: (b) "Purchased Assets" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.1 of the Purchase Agreement ... Alternatively ... add ...: "The Purchased Assets do not include the Excluded Assets."
reason: Issue 1 identifies the right problem. Bill of Sale § 1.1(b) independently defines 'Purchased Assets' as all assets 'used or held for use in the Business.' It does not carve out the Excluded Assets, and the Bill of Sale's own definition overrides its fallback to the APA. The memo explains why this matters to Marrowind: the operative conveyance instrument could transfer the cash, the Albany facility and the HOLLIS trademark, all of which Seller is retaining. Issue 6 ties this to APA § 10.12, noting that each ancillary agreement 'controls as to its specific subject matter.' The fix adopts the APA § 2.1 definition, which itself excludes the Excluded Assets, and offers an express exclusion sentence as an alternative. The substance of the criterion is met.
